chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to one of his inheritors that he had a debt upon himself. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the deceased was pleased (with the other heirs regarding the debt), then give it to the one to whom he bequeathed it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a debt bequeathed to an heir in a will?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedure for settling a debt owed to an heir when acknowledged in a will, specifically noting the condition of the deceased's state ('mardan' or pleased/sick) as a criterion for validity. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that such bequests are treated as debt repayments rather than part of the fixed inheritance shares, ensuring the heir receives their due before the remaining estate is distributed among all heirs. The context reflects the practical application of *al-wasiyya* (bequest) within the broader framework of *al-mirath* (inheritance), emphasizing fairness and the prevention of dispute among heirs.
